newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares close steady but profit-taking seen.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares close steady but profit-taking seen.

text.p: Leading Russian shares ended steady on Monday after partially recovering from opening weakness but traders forecast further profit-taking would drive the market lower for a few weeks.

"The general tendency is to further weakening of the market," said Renaissance Capital trader Vladimir Chkhikvadze. "There probably will not be any growth for a few weeks...and volumes will decline in the near future."
The Russian Trading System 22-share index closed down 3.61 percent from Friday's finish at 475.54 on $55.51 million total market turnover, low compared to recent activity.

National power utility UES rose to $0.4285 from a morning low of $0.4100 but off Friday's close of $0.4330, Rostelekom telecoms company dropped to $4.40 from $4.67 and Mosenergo power utility dropped to $1.500 from $1.532.
Traders said a summer lull had begun, coinciding with profit-taking after a month-long rally which lifted the RTS index by about 30 percent.
Foreigners who generally have the strongest influence on the market were relatively inactive and Russian operators were seen as the biggest profit-takers.
"Everyone wants to take profit," said Regent Securities trader Alexander Fonarkov. "This could last until autumn."
He said that second tier shares which some traders had expected would see renewed interest on reallocation from leading shares this week had not seen large volumes.
"Interest in them has weakened, since everyone is looking at the blue chips," he said.
